rem:pre-tau-vs-post-tau:
Remark Archimedean wall discipline: pre-\tau vs post-\tau.

Superseded. The scalar aether density \rho_q = 1/\hbar_q^2 used below is the structurally-wrong leading-order ansatz; the operator-valued form supersedes it (mass-endomorphism-tower).

The Archimedean wall. Every derivation step belongs to exactly one of two registers:

Register Coefficient ring Operative invariants Examples
Pre-\tau R = \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}, (q-q^{-1})^{-1}] (or z-Habiro) Hecke spectra, Markov traces SDP feasibility, Gröbner--Shirshov reductions
Post-\tau \mathbb{R} via \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} Hyperbolic volumes PL thimble flow, Bloch--Wigner D(z)

The functor \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} is the only legal bridge between these columns.

  • Pre-\tau derivation steps cannot use post-\tau values (e.g., hyperbolic volume) as inputs.
  • Post-\tau derivation steps cannot claim algebraic-side identities (e.g., Hecke relations) that only hold prior to realization.
  • Bridging equalities that cross the wall must use \approx unless stating an explicit error term. They describe the functor, not algebraic derivation steps.

Motivic shorthand. The z-Habiro completion houses algebraic encounter data, treating quantum dilogarithm poles as quotients of cyclotomic ideals. Under \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}, these algebraic poles realize as hyperbolic-triangulation cusps. Any violation of the wall boundary breaks the formal derivation.
rem:vol-as-motivic-period:
Remark \mathrm{Vol}(K) as a motivic period: the Bloch--Wigner regulator reading of \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}. Period interpretation. The hyperbolic volume \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K) is a motivic period: the value of a mixed-Tate motive under the Bloch-Wigner regulator r_\infty. For a hyperbolic knot complement with shape parameters z_i, the volume is:

  \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K)
  \;=\;
  \sum_{i=1}^{k} D(z_i),

where D is the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm. Each D(z_i) is a Kontsevich-Zagier period. For motivic periods and the action of the motivic Galois group on them, in the basic case of the motivic fundamental group of \mathbb{P}^1 \setminus \{0, 1, \infty\}, whose periods are the multiple zeta values, see [brown-motivic-p1-three-points, §1].

Regulator interpretation. The shape parameters define a class [K] \in \mathcal{B}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) in the pre-Bloch group, yielding:

  \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K)
  \;=\;
  r_\infty\bigl([K]\bigr).

The volume \mathrm{Vol}(K) is the K-theoretic image of an algebraic class under a transcendental regulator.

QOU placement. The archimedean realization functor factorizes across three pictures: adelic projection (\pi_\infty \circ \tau), Euler-characteristic integration (\pi_\infty \circ \chi_{\mathrm{top}}), and Bloch-Wigner regulation (r_\infty). These pictures agree on the algebraic quantum volume domain. Each formalizes a distinct aspect: adelic ensures categorical compatibility, Euler-characteristic handles blow-up calculus, and Bloch-Wigner bridges to quantum topology literature.
rem:kashaev-as-archimedean-realization:

Algebraic side. The colored Jones polynomial evaluated at roots of unity is a purely p-adic/cyclotomic discrete algebraic trace. The algebraic quantum volume \mathrm{Vol}_q(\mathcal{B}_K) packages these local data into a global Habiro element.

  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\bigl(\mathrm{Vol}_q(\mathcal{B}_K)\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}}\bigl(\mathrm{Vol}_q(\mathcal{B}_K)\bigr).

The fibre functor \tau is the exclusive archimedean route.
def:phi-q-piece: Definition Φ_q-piece sub-link K_S of a braid closure. Let \beta \in B_n be a braid. For each subset S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-2\}, the \Phi_q-piece K_S \subseteq S^3 is the link obtained from \widehat{\beta} by L_0-smoothing every crossing not in S while leaving crossings in S intact.
rem:phi-q-piece-remark:
Remark Properties and motivic interpretation of the Φ_q-pieces. This construction satisfies three properties:

  1. Functoriality: K_\emptyset is the unlink; K_{\{0,\dots,n-2\}} is the original closure.
  2. Subset compatibility: K_S = (K_T)_S for S \subseteq T.
  3. Categorical interpretation: The pieces K_S constitute the geometric shadow of the Wedderburn-block stratification. The algebraic spectral coordinate \prod_{i \in S} \hat{V}_i localizes geometrically to K_S.

The piece K_S acts as the geometric carrier of the per-S summand \Phi_q\bigl(\bigl\lvert\prod_{i \in S} \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{full}}\bigr\rvert\bigr). The empty piece is the descended level-zero carrier. All others are transient carriers. The \Phi_q-piece serves as the discrete unit on which archimedean realization evaluates the tower.

The quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q is a q-deformation of the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm. The per-piece summand \Phi_q(\lvert V_S\rvert) represents a class in the quantum Bloch group. The family \{K_S\}_S provides the geometric stratification along which the regulator decomposes, solidifying the bridge to hyperbolic volume as a strict regulator statement.
prop:phi-q-tower-algebraic-stratificatio:
Proposition Algebraic stratification of the Φ_q tower in H_n(R, q) (no 3-manifold language).

Superseded. The scalar aether density \rho_q = 1/\hbar_q^2 used below is the structurally-wrong leading-order ansatz; the operator-valued form supersedes it (mass-endomorphism-tower).

Proposition (algebraic stratification of the \Phi_q tower). Let \beta \in B_n be a braid, and assume pentagon ascension in the following form (jet-tower remark §"Pentagon ascension"). The sum of the strata with |S| \geq 3 equals a correction \delta_S on the strata with |S| \leq 2, plus a residual lying in the submodule J_{n+1} of contributions at jet level n+1. Then, modulo J_{n+1}, the \Phi_q-tower admits a purely algebraic stratification by |S|, with each summand below read as corrected by \delta_S:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \;=\;
  \bigl\| \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_\emptyset))\bigr\|_F
  \;+\;
  \sum_{|S| = 1} \Phi_q\bigl(\|\hat V_S\|_F\bigr)
  \;+\;
  \sum_{|S| = 2} z^{2} \Phi_q\bigl(\|\hat V_S\|_F\bigr).

The Frobenius norm \|\cdot\|_F evaluates entirely within the ground ring \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}].

If every stratum with |S| \geq 3 is zero, one can take \delta = 0 and J_{n+1} = 0, and the identity holds exactly. The statement is conditional on pentagon ascension, which is not proved. Stated without \delta and J_{n+1}, the hypothesis is empty: every sum satisfies it with \delta = 0 and J_{n+1} the whole ring. Its content is the pentagon identity that produces \delta, and the jet-level tower that defines J_{n+1}. One candidate for the residual submodule comes from the jet module of order k, (S \otimes S)/I^{k+1}, where I = \ker(m : S \otimes S \to S). There the residual submodule is I^{k+1}. At first order it is I^2, and the conclusion is an equality in J^1(S) = (S \otimes S)/I^2. The jet order k is not the tower level n. The tower iterates first jets, and J^1(J^1(S)) is not (S \otimes S)/I^3, so I^{k+1} is not J_{n+1}. Which submodule is J_{n+1} at tower level n+1 is open. The candidate does not show that the |S| \geq 3 residual lies in I^2, and it does not show that a stratum value lies in S \otimes S. Each stratum \Phi_q(\|\hat V_S\|_F) is a scalar in the ground ring. Placed in S \otimes S as a scalar, it lies in I only if it is zero, whenever the ground ring embeds in S. So for scalar strata the condition "residual in I^{k+1}" is the same as "residual zero". A residual that is nonzero but lies in I^2 needs strata that are not scalars, such as jets built from \hat V_S itself rather than from its norm. Such non-scalar jet strata have not yet been constructed, nor has an explicit inter-level jet-prolongation lift been exhibited on concrete algebras. Not proved either: that the |S|-grading coincides with the J^{|S|}/J^{|S|+1} grading of the GS confinement filtration.

The algebraic stratification operates strictly pre-\tau. It decomposes the mass endomorphism using only discrete categorical data, isolating the structural descent without invoking any hyperbolic or continuous geometry.
prop:mass-endomorphism-tower:
Proposition Proton--electron mass endomorphism tower (z = q^3/(q^2+1), \mathrm{Li}_2^q): the mass formula is positive under a genuine norm and bounded dilogarithm. The mass of a vortex \varrho with braid representative \beta \in B_n and n - 1 generators evaluates as:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  =
  \Bigl\lvert \prod_{i=0}^{n-2} \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{full}} \Bigr\rvert
  -
  \sum_{i=0}^{n-2}
    \mathrm{Li}_2^q\!\bigl(-\lvert\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{full}}\rvert\bigr)
  -
  \sum_{0 \leq i < j \leq n-2}
    z^2 \cdot \mathrm{Li}_2^q\!\bigl(-\lvert\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{full}}
      \cdot \hat{V}_j^{\mathrm{full}}\rvert\bigr),

where z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) is the Markov parameter and \mathrm{Li}_2^q is the symmetric q-dilogarithm \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) = \sum_{n \geq 1} z^n / (n \cdot [n]_q).

The three sums isolate the three types of blow-up centers in the brane tower. The descended term is the base-level regular-representation trace. The single-generator blow-ups and the pair blow-ups apply the \mathrm{Li}_2^q functional across the generator loci. The weight z^2 for pairs strictly follows from the Markov-trace factorization.

The comparison at q_0 behind the choice of \mathrm{Li}_2^q over the Faddeev \Phi_q form is recorded in this remark.
rem:mass-endomorphism-tower-phi-q-histor: Remark Why \mathrm{Li}_2^q replaced the Faddeev \Phi_q form in the mass tower. Choice of the q-dilogarithm convention (\mathrm{Li}_2^q versus \Phi_q). In the mass-endomorphism tower, the series is resummed through the Jackson q-dilogarithm \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) rather than the compact Faddeev function \Phi_q(z). Direct term-by-term q-integration of the geometric series produces \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z), which preserves bar-involution isospin symmetry at the real aether anchor q_0 and avoids the mirror-nucleus asymmetry poles introduced by the modular double ratio in \Phi_q.
prf:mass-endomorphism-tower:
Proof Proof of mass endomorphism tower. The Hecke mass element \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) \in H_n(R, q) (Hecke mass element) decomposes via the descent involution into descended and transient contributions. The transient trace localises to blow-up centres p in the brane tower (topological decomposition); integrating the q-deformed expansion flow \ln_q(1+t)/t along the radial coordinate of the Briggs--Klein chart (Briggs--Klein chart) over each resolved defect E_i \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) yields the symmetric q-dilogarithm:

  \int_0^{V} \frac{\ln_q(1+t)}{t}\,dt
  \;=\; -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-V),
  \qquad
  \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) := \sum_{n \geq 1} \frac{z^n}{n \cdot [n]_q},

where [n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n})/(q - q^{-1}) is the symmetric q-integer.

Subproof. The q-deformed natural log has Taylor series \ln_q(1-z) = -\sum_{n\geq 1} z^n/[n]_q ([definition of q-log]). Termwise differentiation of \mathrm{Li}_2^q gives*

  \frac{d}{dz}\mathrm{Li}_2^q(z)
  = \sum_{n \geq 1} \frac{z^{n-1}}{[n]_q}
  = -\frac{\ln_q(1-z)}{z}.

Integrating from 0 to z (with \mathrm{Li}_2^q(0) = 0): \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) = -\int_0^z (\ln_q(1-u)/u)\,du. Substituting u = -t, z = -V:

  \mathrm{Li}_2^q(-V)
  = -\int_0^{-V}\!\frac{\ln_q(1-u)}{u}du
  = -\int_0^{V}\!\frac{\ln_q(1+t)}{t}dt

so \int_0^V (\ln_q(1+t)/t)\,dt = -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-V). \square_{\text{sub}}

canonical structural verification: the integration value matches -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-V) to all displayed digits at q_0 \approx 1.110 for V \in \{0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.85, 0.95, 0.989\} .

The integral is not the compact quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q(V) = \prod_{k\geq 1}(1 - q^{-k}V)^{-1}, whose logarithm uses asymmetric q-integers (q^n - 1). Both \mathrm{Li}_2^q and \log\Phi_q are q-deformations of the classical dilogarithm, but they use different q-integer conventions; the Hecke setting requires the symmetric form [n]_q, so \mathrm{Li}_2^q is the correct identification.

The NF basis of H_n(R, q) decomposes by generator content. Each subset S \subseteq \{0,\dots,n-2\} contributes a blow-up centre with spectral coordinate \prod_{i\in S}\hat{V}_i and Markov weight z^{|S|}; triples and higher generator subsets are not independent at level n (they ascend to jet level n+1 via the pentagon closure of \Phi_q, see quantum Bloch group). The independent order-1 and order-2 subsets enumerate exactly the singleton and pair sums above.

For the adjacent pair \{i, i+1\} the NF elements \sigma_i\sigma_{i+1} and \sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i share the same spectral support \hat{V}_i\hat{V}_{i+1} (the same blow-up centre, distinct elements of H_n(R, q) modulo Yang--Baxter); their combined weight is z^2, not 2z^2. For a non-adjacent pair \{i, j\} with \lvert i-j\rvert\geq 2 far-commutativity gives \sigma_i\sigma_j = \sigma_j\sigma_i and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i\sigma_j) = z \cdot z = z^2 — a single NF element supporting a single blow-up centre. In every case the combined pair weight is z^2. Summing over all pairs i<j gives the claimed quadratic term.

The element \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 is not an independent blow-up centre: it decomposes as \sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1 via Yang--Baxter, the same transient support as the adjacent pair. Higher-order subsets of size \geq 3 are similarly subsumed — not into level-n singletons and pairs, but into the level-(n{+}1) jet contribution via the pentagon identity of the quantum dilogarithm (for the explicit ascension see jet-tower reformulation). \square
prf:quantum-dilog-convergence:
Proof Proof of quantum dilog convergence. Each factor is non-zero on the domain: \lvert q^{-k} z\rvert < q^{-k} \cdot q = q^{\,1-k} \leq 1 for k \geq 1, so 1 - q^{-k} z \neq 0 (quantum dilogarithm). Writing a_k = q^{-k} z, the geometric series \sum_{k \geq 1} \lvert a_k\rvert = \lvert z\rvert \sum_{k\geq 1} q^{-k} converges since q > 1. On the domain every denominator obeys the uniform lower bound 1 - a_k \geq 1 - \lvert z\rvert / q > 0, so the deviation terms g_k = (1 - a_k)^{-1} - 1 = a_k/(1 - a_k) satisfy \lvert g_k\rvert \leq \lvert a_k\rvert /(1 - \lvert z\rvert/q) and are summable by comparison. Multipliability of \prod_k (1 + g_k) = \prod_k (1 - a_k)^{-1} then follows from the one-plus-summable criterion for infinite products. \square

This is the convergence half of the brane-tower programme — the claim of brane tower in z-Habiro that survives the refutation of the level-selection rule n_\star. It establishes that \Phi_q is a genuine analytic object on \lvert z\rvert < q, so the z-Habiro Cauchy-limit construction has a well-defined target.

Note (scope). Convergence does not make the per-generator \Phi_q(\lvert\hat V_i\rvert) form a production mass input. At the physical brane-tower argument z_i = \lvert\hat V_i^{\mathrm{full}}\rvert \in [0.85, 1) the product is convergent but enormous (\Phi_q(0.989) \approx 6.7 \times 10^5), which is why the canonical mass tower mass-endomorphism tower evaluates the bounded symmetric form -\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-\lvert\hat V_i\rvert) rather than \Phi_q. The proposition closes the analytic existence question, not the regularization question.
rem:motivic-mass-rationale:
Remark Why a motivic measure: singular intermediate states and the archimedean realization. The mass endomorphism (proton--electron mass ratio) must assign a finite, q-discrete weight to a Gröbner--Shirshov reduction whose intermediate states are singular: there is no smooth volume form to integrate, no measure-theoretic Lebesgue construction that survives the blow-up. The motivic measure \mu of def:motivic-mass-measure assigns each reduction step a value in the Grothendieck ring \mathcal{M}, purely algebraically, by tracking which classes of varieties appear as exceptional fibers. The categorical analogue of crossing the \chi_{\mathrm{eu}}(M_0) = -6 topological horizon (topological mass formula) is exactly the contribution [E_i^{\circ}] \mathbb{L}^{-d_i} of the exceptional divisor of that blow-up.

The motivic mass \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{mot}}(\beta) is a class in \widehat{\mathcal{M}} — a motive, not yet a real number. The real-valued physical mass is recovered by applying the archimedean realization functor, constructed later in this chapter once the adelic base ring it projects from is in place.

Mass from blow-ups. When the categorical Gröbner--Shirshov reduction (three-parameter Wedderburn formula) processes a braid \beta \in H_n(R, q), it performs a finite sequence of algebraic blow-ups of the brane variety X along the crossing loci, producing exceptional divisors E_1, \dots, E_r with multiplicities (or codimension weights) d_1, \dots, d_r. The topological mass of the reduced state is the motivic integral of the trivial function over the arc space, computed by Kontsevich's change-of-variables formula as

  \mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{mot}}(\beta)
  \;:=\;
  \int_{\mathcal{L}(X)} d\mu
  \;=\;
  \sum_{i=1}^{r}\, [E_i^{\circ}] \, \mathbb{L}^{-d_i}
  \;\in\;\widehat{\mathcal{M}},

where [E_i^{\circ}] is the class of the smooth open part of the i-th exceptional divisor.
conj:kashaev-volume-conjecture:
Conjecture Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture.

Superseded. The scalar aether density \rho_q = 1/\hbar_q^2 used below is the structurally-wrong leading-order ansatz; the operator-valued form supersedes it (mass-endomorphism-tower); the canonical replacement is the operator-valued A^\lambda_{\mu, \nu}(I) graded expansion graded expansion of \rho_K.

The Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture (KVC) asserts that, for every hyperbolic knot K \subseteq S^3, the Kashaev limit of the colored Jones polynomial computes the hyperbolic volume of the complement,

  \mathrm{Vol}_{\mathrm{hyp}}(S^3 \setminus K)
  \;=\;
  2\pi \cdot \lim_{N \to \infty}
  \frac{\log \lvert J_N(K)\rvert}{N},
  \qquad
  J_N(K)\big\vert_{q = \exp(2\pi i / N)},

with the convention that the right-hand side vanishes when K is not hyperbolic. KVC was conjectured by Kashaev [kashaev1997] and reformulated in terms of the colored Jones polynomial by Murakami–Murakami [murakami-murakami2001]. It is open in general (proved only for specific families: the figure-eight knot, certain torus and pretzel knots, etc.).

Inside QOU, KVC is the consistency statement that the archimedean realisation functor \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} = \pi_\infty \circ \tau (archimedean realization functor) applied to the algebraic quantum volume (algebraic quantum volume) recovers the hyperbolic volume; this is the content of the per-block Kashaev as archimedean realization remark.

KVC as an explicit hypothesis

KVC is used throughout as an explicit hypothesis. Every downstream result that depends on it is conditional on KVC — and only on KVC restricted to the knots involved: a bridge statement of the form \Phi_q(V_S) = \rho_q \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(K_S) depends only on KVC for K_S. Such a result becomes unconditional for a knot family (figure-eight, torus, etc.) exactly where KVC is actually proved.

The conjecture itself remains open at the level of \pi_0 — no claim of proof is made by stating it as a hypothesis.

Motivic perspective

KVC is, in motivic language, a regulator statement: the hyperbolic volume of S^3 \setminus K is the image of a class in the Bloch group \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{C}) under the Borel/Beilinson regulator r_\infty, and the colored Jones polynomial at q = \exp(2\pi i / N) is the q-deformed avatar of that class [zagier1986, neumann-zagier1985]. The QOU recasting frames \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} = \pi_\infty \circ \tau as the archimedean realisation functor on the algebraic data \Phi_q(\lvert V_S\rvert) — a class in the quantum Bloch group (quantum Bloch group) — landing in \mathbb{R} as the hyperbolic volume of the corresponding Φ_q-piece. KVC, in this presentation, is the assertion that the q-deformed regulator agrees with the classical one in the Kashaev limit.

Two published neighbours of the statement

Gukov's generalised volume conjecture is a one-parameter family that contains this statement. It predicts the limit of \log J_N(K, e^{2\pi i/k})/k as N, k \to \infty with N/k fixed, as \tfrac{1}{2\pi}\big(\mathrm{Vol}(l,m) + i\,2\pi^2\,\mathrm{CS}(l,m)\big) evaluated on the zero locus of the A-polynomial, and it reduces to the volume conjecture at m = 1 [arxiv-hep-th-0306165v1, §5.2, eqs. (5.12)--(5.13)]. For 4_1 the source checks the real part of the family [arxiv-hep-th-0306165v1, §5.3]. The figure-eight case of the conjecture above is therefore the m = 1 member of that family.

Baseilhac and Ben Aribi prove a volume-conjecture statement for the quantum hyperbolic invariants H_N(M,\rho,h_\rho,k_c) of the figure-eight complement M, for odd N \ge 3. Three candidate identifications, in order of plausibility

Candidate 1: hyperbolic 4-manifold volume on a Bring-natural cusped quotient

Goncharov (1995, 2002) and Beilinson–Levin connect \mathrm{Li}_3 values at algebraic points to volumes of hyperbolic 4-manifolds via the regulator K_5^{\mathrm{ind}}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) \otimes \mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{R}/\pi^4 \mathbb{Q}. A specific 4-manifold is needed:

Candidate 2: Chern–Simons of an icosahedrally-symmetric knot in S^3

The icosahedral group A_5 \subset S_5 acts on \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) with three orbits of size 12, 20, 30 (the icosahedral configuration). Knots whose holonomy representation lands in this A_5-orbit have Chern–Simons invariants whose archimedean evaluation involves \mathrm{Li}_3 at \zeta_5 shape parameters.

Specifically, for a hyperbolic knot K with shape parameters in \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5), the complexified volume

  \mathrm{CS}(K) + i\,\mathrm{Vol}(K) \;\in\; \mathbb{C} / \pi^2 \mathbb{Z}

has imaginary part (volume) at depth 2 and real part (CS) at depth 3. For an A_5-symmetric knot, the depth-3 part should be expressible via \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5) and its Galois conjugates.

Discharge target: identify a knot K with \mathrm{CS}(K) \stackrel{?}{=} \alpha \cdot \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5) + \beta \cdot \zeta(3) + \cdots for explicit \alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{Q}.

Therefore, their CS invariants cannot be expressed as non-trivial \mathbb{Q}-linear combinations of transcendental numbers like \zeta(3) and \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5). This strictly rules out torus knots as direct geometric realisations for this depth-3 period under Candidate 2.

Candidate 3: iterated integral on \overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0, 5}

Goncharov's motivic fundamental groupoid of \mathbb{P}^1 \setminus \{0, 1, \infty\} generalises to \overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0, 5}, the moduli of 5 ordered marked points on \mathbb{P}^1.   \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5),\; \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^2),\;
  \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^3),\; \mathrm{Li}_3(\zeta_5^4) \;\in\; \mathcal{P}_3.

These values lie in \mathrm{MPV}(3,5), the \mathbb{Q}-span of the multiple polylogarithm values of weight 3 and level 5. Its dimension d(3,5) obeys the Deligne–Goncharov motivic upper bound D(3,5) = 3^3 = 27, tightened by finite and regularized double-shuffle standard relations to d(3,5) \le \mathrm{SR}(3,5) = 22, with no unconditional lower bound known, so a \mathbb{Q}-linear identification of \mathrm{Cl}_3(2\pi/5) inside this span comes with no proved independence of the spanning values; for prime levels p \ge 5, including N = 5, the standard relations are conjectured to generate all \mathbb{Q}-linear relations, attaining d(3,5) = 22 [zhao2010-standard-relations, §1.1, §6, §7.4, §9 Table 2, Conj. 9.2].

The three candidates above are conjecturally the same mathematical content viewed through three lenses:

The geometric realisation question is then: which is the canonical representative for the QOU paper's purposes? Candidate 2 is the most directly compatible with the existing knot-theoretic framework; Candidate 1 is the cleanest from the period-theoretic side; Candidate 3 is most general.

rem:vc-as-depth-2-instance:
Remark Volume Conjecture as the depth-2 instance of GS \leftrightarrow period correspondence. The Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture (Kashaev–Murakami–Murakami volume conjecture) admits a clean structural reading inside the graded-Mikusiński framework (GS-depth \leftrightarrow Goncharov period-depth correspondence): it is the depth-2 case.

One-line statement

  \text{Volume Conjecture} \;\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\;
  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}\!\left( G^{(2)}(\mathcal{H}_q) \right)
  \;\xrightarrow{\;\;}\;
  \mathcal{P}_2 \big/ \mathcal{P}_1
  \;=\; \{\text{hyperbolic 3-manifold volumes}\}.

Justification of the reading

The Volume Conjecture asserts that the asymptotic growth of the coloured Jones polynomial J_K^{(N)}(q) at q = e^{2\pi i / N} as N \to \infty equals \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K). The algebraic side (J_K \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]) is field-polymorphic and lives in the aether. The geometric side is a real number, transcendental in general.

In graded-Mikusiński terms:

  • J_K^{(N)} is built by repeated application of the depth-2 grouplike \mathrm{Li}_2^q (Faddeev–Kashaev quantum-dilogarithm decomposition).
  • The asymptotic limit at q = e^{2\pi i / N}, N \to \infty, is the archimedean realization \tau_{\mathrm{arch}} followed by std-part on the surreal envelope.
  • Single-\mathrm{Li}_2 factor \Rightarrow iterated-integral depth 2 \Rightarrow Goncharov period-class \mathcal{P}_2 / \mathcal{P}_1 (Bloch regulator K_3^{\mathrm{ind}}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}) \otimes \mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{R} / \pi^2 \mathbb{Q}).

The Volume Conjecture is therefore not a coincidence: hyperbolic volumes appear at depth 2 because that is structurally where the Bloch–Wigner regulator lives. Predicted at every depth n is an analogous statement: colored quantum invariants built from \mathrm{Li}_n^q asymptote to weight-n Goncharov periods.

Implications of accepting the depth correspondence

The depth correspondence does not prove the Volume Conjecture. What it does is reduce the conjecture to two structurally smaller claims:

  1. Categorical Laplace transport. Show that the asymptotic at roots of unity coincides with the categorical Laplace transform of \Phi_q followed by std-part — i.e. that the limiting procedure is intrinsically the Mikusiński transform applied stratum-by-stratum. Already partially in the paper via Uniqueness of the categorical Laplace transform.
  2. Sharpness at depth 2. Show that the image of G^{(2)} in \mathcal{P}_2 / \mathcal{P}_1 contains the Bloch–Wigner regulator class of every hyperbolic knot complement. This is the modern formulation of Bloch's 1978 conjecture and is a known target in motivic cohomology.

The framework thus does not eliminate the open problem — it places it in its correct depth-graded category, where partial results already exist (Murakami–Murakami 2001 for the figure-8; Garoufalidis–Lê for torus knots; many others).

prop:thurston-volume-additivity:
Proposition Thurston additivity of hyperbolic volume over ideal tetrahedra.

Thurston volume additivity

Every hyperbolic knot complement admits an ideal triangulation by tetrahedra with vertices on the sphere at infinity. A single complex shape parameter z_i determines each tetrahedron up to isometry.

The hyperbolic volume of the knot complement S^3 \setminus \mathcal{K} is the sum of its tetrahedral volumes:

  V(\mathcal{K})
  \;=\;
  \sum_{i = 1}^N D(z_i),

where D(z_i) is the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm evaluated at the shape parameter. Flat tetrahedra (z_i \in \mathbb{R}) contribute zero volume.

The sum does not depend on the ideal triangulation chosen. More generally, for any representation \rho\colon \pi_1(M) \to \mathrm{Isom}^+(\mathbb{H}^3) of a cusped orientable 3-manifold M, the volume of \rho is well defined and equals the volume obtained by straightening any ideal triangulation of M [francaviglia2003, §2].

Braid-theoretic consequence

A knot diagram induces an ideal triangulation containing one tetrahedron per crossing. Consequently, the volume sums additively over crossings:

  V(\mathcal{K}) \;=\; \sum_{\text{crossings } c} D(z_c).

Torus knots project entirely onto a surface, forcing every z_c to be real. Their hyperbolic volume vanishes identically.

Extremality

The Bloch-Wigner function reaches its maximum at the regular shape z = e^{i\pi/3}, yielding the Lobachevsky constant v_3 \approx 1.01494. The figure-eight knot 4_1 comprises exactly two such tetrahedra, producing the minimum hyperbolic volume V(4_1) = 2 v_3 \approx 2.02988. This extremality pins the aether parameter q_0 by calibrating the quantum of action \hbar_q^2.

thm:flat-tetrahedron-zero-volume:
Theorem A flat ideal tetrahedron has zero volume: D(x) = 0 for every real x.

Flat tetrahedra contribute nothing

An ideal tetrahedron with shape parameter z has volume D(z), the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm. The tetrahedron is degenerate, or flat, exactly when z is real: its four ideal vertices 0, 1, \infty, z then lie on a common circle on the sphere at infinity, and it collapses.

For every real x,

  D(x) \;=\; 0 .

No hypothesis on x is required.

Why the unrestricted form is the one worth stating

Writing D in the Lobachevsky form D(z) = \Lambda(\theta_1) + \Lambda(\theta_2) + \Lambda(\theta_3), where the \theta_i are the arguments of the three edge parameters, the proof is immediate: the edge parameters of a real shape are themselves real, the argument of a real number is 0 or \pi, and \Lambda vanishes at both.

That argument never uses the size of x, and the unrestricted statement matters. A version restricted to 0 < x < 1 — the range in which all three edge parameters have the most obvious signs — is strictly weaker, and too weak for the application in the next block: the trefoil's shape parameters are -1 and 2, both outside that interval. The vanishing must hold on all of \mathbb{R} or it does not reach the case it is wanted for.

The two degenerate values are covered as well. At x = 1 the second edge parameter 1/(1-x) is undefined, and at x = 0 the third, 1 - 1/x; under the convention 1/0 = 0 both evaluate to a real number with argument 0, so the formula returns 0 there too.

Consequence

Volume is additive over an ideal triangulation, so a triangulation whose shape parameters are all real has total volume zero. This is the mechanism behind the vanishing of hyperbolic volume for torus knots, and it is used in that form in the block that follows.
thm:gluing-equations-do-not-detect-hyper:
Theorem The gluing equations do not detect hyperbolicity: the trefoil's flat shapes satisfy them exactly.

What the gluing equations do, and do not, decide

An ideal triangulation with shape parameters z_1, \dots, z_N carries Thurston's gluing equations: one equation per edge class, asserting that the edge parameters around that edge multiply to 1. A solution is geometric when every z_i lies in the upper half plane, and only then does the triangulation describe a hyperbolic structure [martelli2016] (Prop.~14.1.7).

It is tempting to treat the equations themselves as the test — to read "the gluing equations are satisfiable" as "the manifold is hyperbolic". They are not that test.

The trefoil complement is Seifert fibred, hence not hyperbolic. Nevertheless its triangulation admits shape parameters

  z_0 \;=\; -1, \qquad z_1 \;=\; 2,

which are rational, satisfy every gluing equation exactly, are all real — hence flat — and give total volume 0.

So a degenerate solution exists and the equations are entirely satisfied by it. What fails is not solvability but positivity.

Why the separation is structural

The two halves of the gluing data behave differently:

condition needs
edge equations \prod z^{a} (z')^{b} (z'')^{c} = 1 z \neq 0, 1 only
dihedral angles summing to 2\pi around each edge \mathrm{Im} z > 0

The edge equations are algebraic identities in \mathbb{C} \setminus \{0,1\} and descend to flat shapes without complaint. The angle conditions do not: the dihedral angles are the arguments of the edge parameters, and a flat tetrahedron has angles 0 and \pi rather than a genuine angle triple summing to \pi. Positivity is what detects hyperbolicity; the equations are indifferent to it.

Other torus knots behave the same way, over the fields one expects

The pattern is uniform, and the fields are the real cyclotomic subfields the torus type predicts:

8_{19}, the (3,4) torus knot 1+\sqrt 2,\; -1+\sqrt 2,\; -1 \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt 2)

These are genuine number fields generated by genuine solutions. They are not shape fields in the sense of Neumann-Reid, which is the invariant trace field of a hyperbolic structure — these manifolds have none. They are the fields of a degenerate solution.

Methodological remark

A pipeline that solves the gluing equations and reports the resulting volume will return 0 here rather than failing, and 0 is a perfectly good number. Any such pipeline therefore needs the positivity check as a separate gate, and needs a non-hyperbolic control to demonstrate that the gate is doing something. Without one, the pipeline cannot distinguish "detected geometry" from "solved a system of equations".
thm:gluing-certification-mechanical-reac:
Theorem The exact gluing verification is mechanical to degree 14 and 14 tetrahedra: neither predicted ceiling exists.

How far the exact gluing verification actually reaches

Shape fields identified from a triangulation give the edge and cusp equations a purely algebraic form: with P the minimal polynomial and each shape z_j = Q_j(\theta) an explicit element of \mathbb{Q}(\theta), the verification lives in \mathbb{Q}[x]/(P) and no numerics enter at any step.

Two consequences make the whole thing mechanical.

Every identity holds at an arbitrary root. Because the computation is in the quotient ring, each equation holds at every root of P, not merely the geometric one. This removes the root-selection problem entirely — otherwise one would have to prove that a quartic or a degree-14 polynomial has a root in the upper half plane before saying anything at all. Which root is geometric is a separate, numerical question.

Every proof is a single deterministic step. Clearing denominators turns \prod z^{a} (z')^{b} (z'')^{c} = 1 into the polynomial identity

  \prod_j z_j^{a_j}\,\prod_j (z_j-1)^{c_j}
  \;=\;
  \prod_j (1-z_j)^{b_j}\,\prod_j z_j^{c_j},

whose difference is divisible by P exactly. The cofactor comes from exact polynomial division and the proof is one linear-combination step; non-vanishing of each z_j and 1-z_j comes from a Bézout certificate. Nothing is guessed, and a wrong candidate fails at generation rather than producing an unprovable claim.

Cusp equations were expected to be harder and are not

Cusp equations carry negative exponents, which suggests they need each parameter's inverse as an explicit polynomial plus integer-power bookkeeping threaded through every statement. They do not. Every edge parameter is a unit, so

  \prod \mathrm{param}^{e} = 1
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \prod_{e>0} \mathrm{param}^{e} \;=\; \prod_{e<0} \mathrm{param}^{-e},

and both sides now carry natural exponents. Clearing denominators reduces the whole thing to the edge case, and no integer-power machinery appears anywhere.

Two predicted ceilings, neither of which exists

The obvious worries about scaling this up are that the certificates grow with the field degree, and that the product over tetrahedra outruns the available finite-product lemmas. Both were expected to bite; both were measured, and neither did.

Degree. The certificates do grow — cofactor degree roughly quadruples and emitted size grows fivefold from degree 4 to degree 9. But the manifold with a degree-14 shape field, whose single largest certificate is over thirty thousand characters, verifies in about two minutes. The naive extrapolation overshoots because cost tracks the number of ring-normalisation calls far more than the size of any one of them. Wide-but-few is cheap.

Tetrahedron count. The finite-product lemmas available off the shelf stop at eight, which reads like a hard limit at nine tetrahedra. It is a limit on the named lemmas, not on the argument: the successor form iterates unaided and unfolds the product at any count. A fourteen-tetrahedron triangulation certifies by the same single step as a two-tetrahedron one.

Net reach: shape-field degrees 2 through 14, triangulations of 2 through 14 tetrahedra, with each manifold's identities assembled into a certificate that the triangulation satisfies its gluing system — not merely a pile of separate equations.

What this does not establish

The identities hold at an arbitrary root, so flat shapes are permitted throughout and hyperbolicity is not established anywhere — that needs \mathrm{Im} z > 0, which is a genuinely separate condition and is exactly the gap the trefoil exhibits: its flat shapes satisfy the edge equations exactly.

Nothing here says any of these triangulations is a triangulation of a knot complement. That is Thurston hyperbolisation together with Mostow rigidity, and it needs a theory of hyperbolic 3-manifolds that this development does not have.

None of the underlying mathematics is new. What is contributed is the exact, mechanically checked form, and the measurement of how far it reaches before anything breaks.
prop:hyperbolic-knot-shape-fields:
Proposition Shape fields of hyperbolic knot triangulations, with the gluing equations verified exactly.

The shape field of a triangulation

For a cusped hyperbolic 3-manifold with an ideal triangulation, the shape field is the number field generated by the tetrahedron shape parameters. By a theorem of Neumann and Reid it coincides with the invariant trace field, so it is an invariant of the manifold rather than of the chosen triangulation.

Because the shapes are algebraic and Thurston's gluing equations — one consistency equation per edge class and two completeness equations per cusp, a solution of which with every \operatorname{Im} z_i > 0 is a complete finite-volume hyperbolic structure [martelli2016] (§14.1, Prop.~14.1.7) — have integer exponents, the whole verification can be carried out exactly, with no floating point: express each shape in \mathbb{Q}(\theta) for a single generator \theta, form \prod_j z_j^{a_j}(z_j')^{b_j}(z_j'')^{c_j} - 1, clear denominators, and reduce modulo the minimal polynomial of \theta. The residual is zero or it is not.

For each knot below, the shape parameters lie in the stated field and satisfy every gluing equation exactly over it.

knot tetrahedra minimal polynomial discriminant
4_1 2 x^2 - x + 1 -3
5_2 3 x^3 - 2x^2 + 3x - 1 -23
6_1 4 x^4 - 3x^3 + 6x^2 - 5x + 2 257
7_2 4 x^5 - 2x^4 + x^3 + 3x^2 - 5x + 3 4409

The figure-eight case is the familiar one: x^2 - x + 1 is the minimal polynomial of a primitive sixth root of unity, so the shape field is the Eisenstein field \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}) and both tetrahedra are regular.

The degree is not bounded by the tetrahedron count

7_2 is triangulated by four tetrahedra and has a quintic shape field. Nothing forces the degree below the number of simplices, and a formalisation sized to the tetrahedron count will be wrong for it. The examples above run from degree 2 to degree 5 on triangulations of two to four tetrahedra.

Stating the identities for an arbitrary root

The verification lives in \mathbb{Q}[x]/(P), so each gluing identity holds at every root of P, not only the geometric one. That is the form in which the identities are proved: for a root t of the minimal polynomial, with each shape written as an explicit polynomial in t,

  \prod_j z_j(t)^{a_j} \cdot \prod_j \bigl(z_j(t) - 1\bigr)^{c_j}
  \;=\;
  \prod_j \bigl(1 - z_j(t)\bigr)^{b_j} \cdot \prod_j z_j(t)^{c_j} ,

the gluing equation with denominators cleared. Stating it this way avoids having to exhibit a root in the upper half plane, which for a quartic or quintic is a substantial obstacle and is not needed for the algebra.

Selecting the geometric root is then a separate, numerical step. It is necessary: a shape field typically carries several Galois-conjugate solutions, and only one of them has all shapes in the upper half plane and reproduces the hyperbolic volume as \sum_j D(z_j).

Scope

Satisfying the gluing equations does not establish that a triangulation is a triangulation of a given knot complement. That is Thurston's hyperbolisation theorem together with Mostow rigidity, and it requires a theory of hyperbolic 3-manifolds which is not developed here. Nor is any statement made about the volume conjecture.

The mathematics recorded here is classical — Thurston, Neumann-Zagier, Neumann-Reid, and the arithmetic-invariant computations of snap. What is contributed is the exact, mechanically checked form.
thm:kummer-bloch-wigner-identity:
Theorem Kummer's identity: D(z) = \mathrm{Im}\,\mathrm{Li}_2(z) + \log\lVert z\rVert\,\arg(1-z) on the upper half plane.

Kummer's identity for the Bloch-Wigner dilogarithm

The volume of an ideal tetrahedron admits two expressions: a sum of Lobachevsky values at its three dihedral angles, and a single dilogarithm expression. They agree.

For every z with \mathrm{Im} z > 0,

  D(z)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{Im}\mathrm{Li}_2(z) \;+\; \log\lVert z\rVert \cdot \arg(1-z) ,

where D(z) = \Lambda(\theta_1) + \Lambda(\theta_2) + \Lambda(\theta_3) is the Lobachevsky sum over the tetrahedron's dihedral angles.

The proof is a rigidity argument, not a computation

The two sides are compared along a ray r \mapsto rz. Their difference has vanishing derivative — and the vanishing is the law of sines for the ideal tetrahedron, \lVert z\rVert = \sin\theta_2 / \sin\theta_3, in disguise. So the difference is constant on the ray. At r = 1 the shape lies on the unit circle, where \log\lVert z\rVert = 0 and both sides reduce to the Clausen value \mathrm{Cl}_2; the constant is therefore zero.

The unit circle is the one place where the identity is visible directly; the radial derivative transports it everywhere else in the upper half plane.

What it buys

The identity is the bridge between the geometric description of tetrahedral volume — angles, Lobachevsky, additivity over a triangulation — and the analytic one, in which volume is an imaginary part of a dilogarithm and the machinery of the five-term identity becomes available. The 5_2 sum rule lives on the analytic side; the triangulation and gluing equations live on the geometric side; this is the map between them.

Scope. The hypothesis \mathrm{Im} z > 0 is genuine and not removable: the right-hand side involves \arg(1-z), which jumps across the real axis. On real shapes both sides vanish, but for a different reason — see the flat-tetrahedron statement.
thm:rivin-concavity-one-tetrahedron:
Theorem Rivin concavity for one ideal tetrahedron: \Lambda(\alpha)+\Lambda(\beta)+\Lambda(\gamma) is strictly concave along every line in the angle simplex.

Concavity of the volume functional

Casson and Rivin's approach to hyperbolic structures replaces the search for shape parameters with a maximisation: an angle structure assigns three positive dihedral angles summing to \pi to each tetrahedron, subject to the linear condition that angles around each edge sum to 2\pi; the hyperbolic structure is the critical point of the total volume on that polytope. The argument needs the volume functional to be concave, or the critical point carries no information.

Let \alpha + \beta + \gamma = \pi and let (u,v,w) be a nonzero tangent direction with u + v + w = 0. Then

  t \;\longmapsto\; \Lambda(\alpha + tu) + \Lambda(\beta + tv) + \Lambda(\gamma + tw)

is strictly concave.

Strict concavity on a convex set is exactly strict concavity along every segment, so this is Rivin's theorem for a single tetrahedron.

The Hessian is computed, not assumed

The proof is via the second derivative, and both derivatives of the Lobachevsky function are established rather than quoted:

  \Lambda'(t) \;=\; -\log\lvert 2\sin t\rvert ,
  \qquad
  \Lambda''(t) \;=\; -\cot t .

So along the line the second derivative is -(u^2\cot\alpha + v^2\cot\beta + w^2\cot\gamma), and strict negativity is a statement about that quadratic form. The quadratic form is the Hessian, derived, rather than a form asserted to be one. With \alpha + \beta + \gamma = \pi and all three angles in (0,\pi), at most one cotangent is negative, and the constraint u+v+w=0 is what forces the combination negative.

What is not claimed

This is concavity for one tetrahedron along one line. Rivin's full theorem — that the total volume over an angle-structure polytope has a unique critical point, and that the critical point is the complete hyperbolic structure — additionally needs the polytope itself, a compactness argument, and the identification of the critical point with a geometric structure. None of that is established here, and the angle-structure polytope for 5_2 is not built.
prop:ideal-tetrahedron-relabelling-invar:
Proposition Relabelling invariance: z \mapsto 1/(1-z) cycles the dihedral angles and preserves volume.

Relabelling an ideal tetrahedron

A shape parameter records a tetrahedron together with a choice of which pair of opposite edges is called first. The map

  z \;\longmapsto\; \frac{1}{1-z}

changes that choice without changing the tetrahedron. Any volume formula written in terms of z must therefore be invariant under it, and if it is not, the formula is measuring the labelling rather than the geometry.

Relabelling cyclically permutes the three dihedral angles, and the volume is unchanged:

  \mathrm{vol}\Bigl(\tfrac{1}{1-z}\Bigr) \;=\; \mathrm{vol}(z) .

The mechanism is that \Lambda(\theta_1) + \Lambda(\theta_2) + \Lambda(\theta_3) is symmetric under cycling its arguments, together with the two identities

  \frac{1}{\,1 - \frac{1}{1-z}\,} = 1 - \frac{1}{z},
  \qquad
  1 - \frac{1}{\;\frac{1}{1-z}\;} = z ,

which say that the second edge parameter of the relabelled tetrahedron is the third of the original, and the third is the first.

Where this is load-bearing

It is what makes the 5_2 volume expression a theorem rather than a coincidence. SnapPy's triangulation of 5_2 has shapes (y_1,\; 1/(1-y_1),\; y_1) — the middle tetrahedron carries the second edge parameter of y_1, not y_1 itself. An earlier model in this corpus took all three to be y_1 and obtained the right total for a reason it did not state. With relabelling invariance the total 3\,D(y_1) follows from the actual shapes, and the earlier agreement is explained rather than relied upon.

The law of sines

The same structure supplies the metric relation

  \lVert z \rVert \;=\; \frac{\sin\theta_2}{\sin\theta_3} ,

the ideal-tetrahedron law of sines, which is the identity that makes the radial argument in Kummer's identity work: it is exactly the statement that a certain derivative along the ray vanishes.
thm:ideal-tetrahedron-law-of-sines:
Theorem The law of sines for an ideal tetrahedron: \lVert z \rVert = \sin\theta_2 / \sin\theta_3.

The three dihedral angles of a shape

An ideal tetrahedron with shape parameter z in the upper half plane has three dihedral angles, one for each pair of opposite edges, given by the arguments of the three edge parameters:

  \theta_1 = \arg z, \qquad
  \theta_2 = \arg\!\left(\frac{1}{1 - z}\right), \qquad
  \theta_3 = \arg\!\left(1 - \frac{1}{z}\right).

They satisfy \theta_1 + \theta_2 + \theta_3 = \pi, which is what makes the angles those of a Euclidean triangle — the link of an ideal vertex.

For every z with \mathrm{Im}\, z > 0,

  \lVert z \rVert \;=\; \frac{\sin\theta_2}{\sin\theta_3} .

The name is apt: the modulus of the shape is a ratio of sines of the opposite angles, exactly as a side of a Euclidean triangle is.

Why this particular lemma is the one worth isolating

Kummer's identity relates the Bloch–Wigner dilogarithm to a sum of Lobachevsky values. Proved on the unit circle \lVert z \rVert = 1, extending it to general z appears to need a genuine two-variable argument, matching

  dD \;=\; \log\lVert z\rVert \; d\arg(1 - z) \;-\; \log\lVert 1 - z\rVert\; d\arg z

against d\Lambda(\theta) = -\log\lvert 2\sin\theta\rvert \; d\theta in both variables at once.

It does not. Fix \arg z and vary only the modulus along a ray. Then \theta_1 is constant, so \Lambda(\theta_1) contributes nothing to the derivative; the angle sum forces d\theta_3 = -d\theta_2; and the two sides become

  \frac{d}{dr}\bigl(\Lambda(\theta_2) + \Lambda(\theta_3)\bigr)
    = \log\!\frac{\sin\theta_3}{\sin\theta_2}\cdot\frac{d\theta_2}{dr},
  \qquad
  \frac{d}{dr} D = -\log r \cdot \frac{d\theta_2}{dr}.

These agree precisely when r = \sin\theta_2 / \sin\theta_3 — which is the theorem above. So the law of sines is exactly the statement that converts a two-variable problem into a one-variable one, and the basepoint r = 1 is supplied by the already-proved unit-circle case. The general identity then follows in the same "same derivative, pin the constant" shape used elsewhere in this arc.

The form the derivative computation actually consumes is the logarithmic one,

  \log(2\sin\theta_3) - \log(2\sin\theta_2) \;=\; -\log\lVert z\rVert ,

which is the theorem after multiplying both sines by 2 and taking logarithms.

The proof is elementary

No analysis is involved. The identity \sin(\arg x) = \mathrm{Im}\, x / \lVert x \rVert for x \neq 0 applies directly, since z and 1 - z are nonzero on the upper half plane. Applying it to the two edge parameters,

  \sin\theta_2 = \frac{\mathrm{Im}\, z}{\lVert 1 - z\rVert},
  \qquad
  \sin\theta_3 = \frac{\mathrm{Im}\, z}{\lVert z\rVert \cdot \lVert 1 - z\rVert},

and the ratio is \lVert z \rVert on the nose. Both sines are positive on the upper half plane, which is what makes the division safe rather than merely formal.

A numerical illustration, and a normalization that must be stated

For the 5_2 knot the shape satisfies a cubic, and \lVert z \rVert = 1.5247025799\ldots agrees with \sin\theta_2/\sin\theta_3 to full precision.

That number requires care, because "the 5_2 shape" is ambiguous. Two cubics for 5_2 appear in this corpus — x^3 - x^2 + 1 and the saddle cubic y^3 - 2y^2 + 3y - 1 — related by the Landen map. They generate the same field, of discriminant -23, but they are not the same polynomial and their roots have different moduli: the upper-half-plane root of the first has modulus \approx 1.1510, of the second \approx 1.5247. The value quoted above is the saddle-cubic root. A modulus is a property of a chosen root, not of the field, so the normalization has to travel with the number.

Scope

This is one lemma about one ideal tetrahedron. It is not new mathematics: the ideal-tetrahedron angle structure is Thurston's, and the dilogarithm identities are classical, with the shape-field setting due to Neumann and Zagier. What is supplied here is a complete proof and, more usefully, the observation that the general Kummer identity needs only this one-variable reduction rather than a two-variable argument.

As throughout this arc, nothing here establishes that any triangulation is a triangulation of a knot complement — that is Thurston hyperbolisation together with Mostow rigidity, which needs a theory of hyperbolic 3-manifolds not developed here. No volume conjecture is touched.
